kind: PRODUCT fix, authored from two MAJORs found while closing the phase-13 e2e gate (C-084). Both defects make §3.7's wedge detector — which the plan calls 'the ONLY wedge detector' — permanently inert on paths that had never run end to end, so a run can sit in EXECUTING forever with no human-readable artifact. That outcome is the exact failure §2.9 says the design exists to close.
authoredBy: orchestrator — authored after reading plan §2.9 (896-915) and §3.7 (1455-1478) directly and verifying both defects in the source: adapter/continuation.ts:743-750, core/gates-phase.ts:173, core/stops.ts:102-131, plugin/index.ts's event hook.
bindings: Discharges nothing from the manifest; it repairs product behaviour the phase-13 e2e first exercised. It also unblocks acceptance row 13.1-s5-report-refuses-dependent-unsettled, which spec SG-4 wrote FOR the blocked-dependency shape and which the product currently cannot reach — C-084 records the e2e's deviation to an independent sibling as a consequence of this defect, to be reverted once this lands.
verifiedAgainstHead: PLAN §2.9:911-915 states the closed failure shape verbatim: 'conductor_report refuses while an item is unpublished-and-unblocked -> the continuation engine re-prompts -> nothing changes -> noop -> and the run ends with no human-readable artifact at all'. That is the shape this fix restores detection of.

PLAN §3.7.1:1459-1463 gates re-prompting on ACTIONABLE WORK, not on a recommended tool: 'session.idle fires for the orchestrator session while run.state is non-terminal AND ACTIONABLE WORK EXISTS (items not PUBLISHED/blocked, or a legal next run transition) => continuation.ts re-prompts'. In the wedge, the dependent item is neither PUBLISHED nor blocked, so actionable work EXISTS by the plan's own definition.

PLAN §3.7.2:1464-1472 — 'futileRePrompts reaching 3 => the engine consults shouldTerminate, records stop noop plus a disengage anomaly, WRITES THE STOP-REPORT (§2.9), and stops re-prompting'. And: 'This counter is the ONLY wedge detector'. A branch that prevents the counter from ever moving disables the only detector there is.

adapter/continuation.ts:743-750 — the SG-2 branch. `const recommended = gate.recommended; if (recommended === null) { journal.log('info','continuation','idle',...); return { runId, prompted: false, stop: null }; }`. Its stated reasoning is sound and must be PRESERVED for the case it was written for: 'prompting a tool nobody offered would invent state; counting it as a futile RE-prompt would be a lie, because nothing was re-prompted.' The defect is that it fires for a case the plan says IS actionable.

core/gates-phase.ts:173 isSettled = state PUBLISHED || blocked !== null || deferred !== null. A LONE blocked item is therefore SETTLED and its run closes `done`; the wedge needs a second, unsettled item behind it.

core/gates-phase.ts cannotEverPublish deliberately does NOT treat a BLOCKED dependency as permanently stuck ('a question can be answered and the item resumes'), so the dependent is neither settled nor stuck: allSettled is false and conductor_report CORRECTLY refuses. That half is right and must not change.

core/gates-phase.ts depsReady excludes the dependent from nextWave while its blocker is not PUBLISHED, and excludes the blocker because it is blocked — so wave.parallel is empty and gate.recommended is null. That half is right and must not change either.

legalTools in the wedge returns 'EXECUTING: no item is schedulable this wave and no report is due; the meta tools remain (§3.2, §4.2)'. So a LEGAL action does exist — conductor_answer against the §2.11 question the blocked item minted, conductor_defer, conductor_status. The re-prompt has something true to name and need not invent a stage tool.

core/stops.ts:84 FUTILE_RE_PROMPT_LIMIT = 3 and :113-115 `if (counters.futileRePrompts >= FUTILE_RE_PROMPT_LIMIT) return { stop: true, kind: 'noop' }`. The terminal rule is ALREADY correct and already reached by shouldTerminate; nothing in core needs to change for defect 1. The counter simply never increments.

core/stops.ts:12-18 STOP_KINDS is a CLOSED vocabulary: done, noop, blocked, surfaced, env, interrupt. §2.9 assigns `env` to 'tooling broken (verify cannot run, server down, fan-out env-failure, override budget exhausted)'. No new kind may be invented for defect 2.

plugin/index.ts's event hook passes `input.client as unknown as ContinuationClient` with NO shape check. With a client whose session.prompt throws (e.g. `{}`), handleSessionIdle sets sent=false and deliberately charges nothing — 'an accusation against a session that was never asked once'. That decision is right per-pass and must be preserved; what is missing is a FLOOR across passes.

§2.9's normative rule, which both halves of this fix must honour: 'Every stop writes a report. Recording a stop is not a terminal action on its own: the recorder MUST invoke the report writer in stop-report mode before the run goes quiet.' And a stop-report 'does NOT re-run the full verify'.
specGaps: FW-SG-1 (what the re-prompt SAYS when no stage tool is offered). §3.7.1 asks for 'a minimal message naming the exact next tool call (derived from gates-phase.ts — the same single source as the injection)'. In the wedge no STAGE tool is legal but the META tools are, and legalTools already says so in its own words. RESOLUTION: the re-prompt names what legalTools actually returns for this position. It must NOT name a stage tool the gate did not offer — that was the SG-2 branch's real concern and it stays honoured.

FW-SG-2 (defect 2's stop kind is not a free choice). STOP_KINDS is closed. A transport that cannot carry a prompt is tooling broken, which §2.9 assigns to `env`; that is the only kind whose definition covers it. RESOLUTION: `env`, with the reason naming the transport failure. Inventing a kind, or reusing `noop` (which means 'no observable progress' and would misreport a run whose orchestrator was never reachable), is forbidden.

FW-SG-3 (the per-pass charge stays zero). Defect 2's fix must NOT start charging idleRePrompts/futileRePrompts for failed sends — the source's reasoning is correct that a session which was never asked cannot be accused of failing to progress. The floor is a SEPARATE consecutive-failure count, and a single transient failure followed by a success must reset it and stop nothing.

FW-SG-4 (this fix does not touch the report tool's refusal). conductor_report REFUSING while the dependent is unsettled is correct behaviour and is not in scope. What is in scope is that the run then gets an artifact instead of going quiet forever.

assertions.text: the §3.7.1 condition is ACTIONABLE WORK, not a recommended stage tool: with item A blocked (test repair exhausted, §2.11 question minted) and item B carrying dependsOn:[A] — B neither PUBLISHED nor blocked nor deferred — a session.idle through the REAL plugin bus hook RE-PROMPTS the orchestrator. Asserted by driving the plugin's own event hook, never by calling handleSessionIdle directly: a test that calls the engine proves the engine works and proves nothing about whether anything reaches it

the wedge now ENDS: three futile idle passes in that shape drive counters.idleRePrompts and counters.futileRePrompts to 3 (identical run-state signature each time), the fourth pass records stop {kind:'noop'} plus a §2.8 disengage anomaly, the run becomes terminal to isTerminal, and a FIFTH pass — waited past the real §3.7.4 debounce so its silence is a decision and not a dropped call — produces no further continuation:reprompt journal record. This is plan §3.7.2's rule reaching the one shape §2.9:911-915 calls the worst failure of the original design

§2.9's normative 'every stop writes a report' holds on this path: report.md is written in stop-report mode with the noop kind as its headline, naming the blocked item A with its exact question id from questions.jsonl, B's unfinished disposition, and any abandoned red test newly added to the §2.11 registry — and NO closing verify is run for it, proved by comparing evidence.jsonl BYTE FOR BYTE across the whole wedge path rather than by counting verify records (a count of 0 === 0 is vacuous)

the SG-2 branch's real concern is honoured rather than discarded: the re-prompt names an action legalTools ACTUALLY returns for this position (the meta tools — conductor_answer against A's open question, conductor_defer, conductor_status) and names NO stage tool, because no stage tool is offered. Asserted by deriving the legal set from core/gates-phase.ts legalTools for the persisted run and requiring the prompt text to intersect it and to be disjoint from the stage tools it excludes — never by matching a string typed into the test

the fix does NOT become 're-prompt always': when there is genuinely no actionable work — every item PUBLISHED, blocked or deferred, and no legal next run transition — the engine still does NOT re-prompt and still charges NO futile count, exactly as the SG-2 branch does today. Both directions asserted in one test, because a change that made the engine prompt unconditionally would satisfy every other row here and would be wrong

a client whose session.prompt throws can no longer disable the detector forever: consecutive transport failures are COUNTED, and at the floor the run records a stop from the CLOSED §2.9 vocabulary — `env`, the kind whose definition covers tooling broken (FW-SG-2) — with the reason naming the transport failure, and writes the stop-report. Asserted with a client that always throws, driving idle passes until the run stops, and requiring isTerminal true at the end

the per-pass accounting is unchanged (FW-SG-3): a failed send still leaves idleRePrompts and futileRePrompts untouched and does not advance lastRePromptMs — a session that was never successfully asked is not accused of failing to progress — and a SINGLE transient failure followed by a successful pass RESETS the consecutive-failure count and stops nothing. Both halves asserted, because a fix that stopped the run on the first transport hiccup would be worse than the defect

the transport stop is legible to the human who has to act on it: a §2.8 anomaly is recorded naming the transport failure, the stop-report's headline carries the env kind and its reason, and the failure is journaled at error level — so a run whose orchestrator became unreachable reports that fact rather than leaving an error line per idle event as its only trace
